newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola approves official post for Savimbi.
newsitem.headline: Angola approves official post for Savimbi.

text.p: The Angolan parliament on Tuesday approved legislation granting former rebel chief Jonas Savimbi official status as opposition leader, paving the way for the creation of a government of national unity on Friday.
A total of 120 members of the assembly voted for the measure, with none opposing and six abstaining.
The parliamentary leader of the ruling MPLA, Joao Lourenco, urged his colleagues to support the law "in the higher interests of the country".
Savimbi's UNITA, which went to war against the MPLA on independence in 1975, had threatened to boycott their own parliamentary swearing-in ceremony on Wednesday if the law was not passed.
A government of national unity is due to be sworn in on April 11 in one of the final steps of the reconciliation process which began with a peace treaty in November 1994.

The legislation formally makes Savimbi president of the largest opposition party and gives him, among other things, the right to regular consultation with the national president and an official residence in Luanda.
